clue.text: Over-complicated airport unfinished with, oddly, no bins

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter of the place name is dropped

parts.note: London's biggest airport

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters of no bins are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about an airport left half-built and fussily designed, with no rubbish bins anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATHROW loses its W to give HEATHRO, then BINSON completes HEATH ROBINSON, the cartoonist famous for absurdly elaborate contraptions.
explanation.definitionFit: William Heath Robinson drew ludicrously elaborate machines, so his name became an adjective for any contraption far more complex than needed.

clue.text: Everyman turned up: pub with green light to restrict sales

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter Everyman refers to himself as me
a bar is a pub
a green light means go

explanation.surface: The setter enjoys a pint, then gets official permission to limit what can be sold.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in a clue usually stands for ME, here read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to embargo is to ban or officially prohibit trade in certain goods, which limits commerce.

clue.text: To admit love in place of worship is symbol of solidarity

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the place of worship takes the love letter inside it

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A statement that letting love into a house of worship expresses unity.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a tennis score of zero is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved totem pole displays a clan's emblems, standing as an emblem of shared kinship and group identity.

clue.text: Cold fish: starters of roach or tail-end of turbot

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so only the initial letters of each word are kept
the tail-end is the back part, so only the closing letters of the fish's name are kept

parts.note: the first letters of roach and or
the last three letters of turbot

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's list: roach or turbot, with talk of a cold fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold fish' seems to belong with the roach and turbot, but it is the definition: an unfeeling person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold fish is an unemotional person, and a robot is a figurative term for someone who acts mechanically without feeling.

clue.text: Restyling stairs with Ben to get handy feature there

indicators.note: restyling gives something a new form, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ben redesigns a staircase and adds something useful to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to the stairs: the definition only makes sense in the context of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Handrails running beside a staircase are useful to grip while climbing, literally a feature for the hand.

clue.text: Recess getting hot in French resort

indicators.note: placed in means one piece goes inside the other, here inside the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A holiday break in a sunny town on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a holiday break, matching the resort, but it means an alcove; H goes between NIC and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow alcove set into a wall, which is exactly what a recess is in architecture.

clue.text: Japanese tradition puts outfit on duck, essentially beaming

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
a rig is an outfit of clothing

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so only the central letters of beaming are kept

parts.note: the three central letters of beaming

explanation.surface: Someone dresses a duck in a costume, smiling broadly all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the outfit goes on, below, the duck; a duck is zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of folding paper into decorative shapes such as cranes.

clue.text: Cake with sharp ends getting commendations

parts.note: a brownie is a small chocolate cake
points are sharp ends, as of pencils

explanation.surface: A cake with spiky edges wins praise from the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownie points are imaginary credits earned for doing something to win favour, a figurative form of praise.

clue.text: Officials needing great blanket to be put on sons

definitions.note: really officers; the clue's word is loose

parts.note: major means great or important
a blanket ban is a general one
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Parents throw a big blanket over their boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket' reads as bedding but is the adjective meaning all-covering; in a down entry, put on means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Major generals are senior army officers ranking above brigadiers, people holding high official rank.

clue.text: Prove the stupidity of 'Jerusalem artichoke turnover'?

indicators.note: a turnover flips something round, so the vegetable's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Jerusalem artichoke is a knobbly tuber

explanation.surface: A sneer at a pastry turnover filled with Jerusalem artichoke as a daft idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' poses as a pastry but signals the reversal; the quotation marks frame it as the absurd dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, showing it to be false or foolish by presenting counter-evidence.

clue.text: Fillet chum — and serve on this

parts.note: to bone a fish is to fillet it
china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, shortened to china

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: fillet the fish, then serve it on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chum' looks like fish bait to go with the fillet, but it means friend: in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is fine porcelain used for dinner services, so it is what food gets served on at the table.

clue.text: Team assembled in factory?

indicators.note: in places the rebuilt letters inside the word for a factory

parts.note: a works is a factory

indicators.note: things assembled are put together from parts, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crew of staff putting products together on a production line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the question mark flags that the full phrase also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleagues who share a workplace function as a group gathered there, so fellow employees in a works are such a crew.

clue.text: Embodiment of love in opera (Tosca)

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the bracketed words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: concealed across the end of opera and the start of Tosca

explanation.surface: Puccini's Tosca as a heroine embodying passionate love.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis invites thoughts of Floria Tosca herself, but the answer lies across op-ERA TO-sca.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek Muse of love poetry, the goddess personifying amorous verse.

clue.text: Rhetorical expression that was taught in Roman kindergartens?

parts.note: surface reading: an early lesson for small children in ancient Rome
setter's reading: Roman numerals use the single stroke letter to represent the number one, a fact young Romans would learn

explanation.surface: A wry guess at the phrases toddlers learned at school in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase states the Roman numeral rule that I stands for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock conversational formula used to declare one's own personal opinion, often emphatically.

clue.text: Distinguished gallery investing in Wacky Races vehicle

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters of the word beside it are scrambled
investing means clothing or surrounding, so the gallery goes inside the other letters

parts.note: races rearranged
the Tate is a renowned London art gallery

explanation.surface: A smart art gallery sponsoring the Wacky Races, the madcap cartoon car contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Wacky Races was a Hanna-Barbera cartoon about a car contest, which hides 'Wacky' as an anagram signal inside a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a British term for a station wagon, a motor car with a long rear load area.

clue.text: In England, choir endlessly making the same sounds

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: ENG is the abbreviation for England

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the singing group is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: An English choir singing in unison, on and on without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In England' reads as a location, but it tells you the choir goes inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something echoing repeats or reverberates a sound, so it keeps producing the identical noise again.

clue.text: Lovely strong swimmer

parts.note: hunky means muscular and strong
the dory is a fish, and fish are swimmers in crosswords

explanation.surface: Admiring a handsome, powerful swimmer at the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a sporting athlete, but it is a fish; John Dory is a familiar species.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is an informal expression meaning everything is fine, satisfactory or excellent.

clue.text: Being sorry, repent 100%

indicators.note: a sorry state is a mess, so the letters are put into disarray

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Being remorseful means repenting wholeheartedly, one hundred per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 100% looks like a single figure of speech, but it splits: 100 is C in the anagram and the % sign is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol is read aloud as two words meaning out of every hundred, its standard spoken form.

clue.text: Woman concerning a certain Boris, we're told

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the tennis player's surname counts by its sound

parts.note: Boris Becker, the German tennis champion

explanation.surface: A woman with some connection to a famous man named Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris' suggests a politician, but Becker, the tennis star, is the one, and in British speech his name rhymes with a short form of a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a female given name, so it stands for any woman so called.

clue.text: Becomes absorbed by invigorating ski inns

indicators.note: invigorating livens things up, so the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets engrossed by bracing mountain lodges at a ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea sinks in it is gradually understood, much as a liquid soaks into a sponge.

clue.text: Fervid respect for symbol of monarchy

indicators.note: fervid means heated and agitated, so the letters are worked up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Passionate reverence for the crown and all it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The sceptre is the ornamental staff a sovereign holds at a coronation as an emblem of royal authority.

clue.text: Emails appear here when genius removes underwear

indicators.note: removing takes something away, so the item of underwear comes off the front

parts.note: a brainbox is a very clever person
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A clever person undresses just as new messages arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAINBOX minus BRA leaves the answer; brainbox is a British informal word for a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: An email program's inbox is the folder where newly received messages are delivered and listed.

clue.text: Gas produced by kiss not at all uplifting

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter

parts.note: none at all means not at all, as in none the wiser

explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a rare, inert noble gas found in tiny amounts in the atmosphere and used in bright lamps.

clue.text: Dry debate regurgitated for childhood companion

indicators.note: regurgitated food comes back up churned, so the letters return in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tedious argument rehashed for the benefit of a young child.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed toy bear is a cuddly plaything many children keep beside them as a comforting friend.

clue.text: 'Doctor' hates to see this beer in Denmark

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the country's abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show the Doctor is Doctor Who, the BBC time traveller, not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Daleks are the robotic alien villains of Doctor Who, the hero's most famous enemy.

clue.text: Industrial demolition of ethnic state

explanation.definitionFit: Technical relates to applied science and engineering, the practical skills of manufacture and industry.

clue.text: Old corsair that's amassed Liberians' first pieces of eight

explanation.definitionFit: Octal notation is a number system with base eight, using only the digits nought to seven.

clue.text: Rampantly keen, as my randy economist

parts.note: taken as written
